Where Niagara County’s money comes from, and where it goes

31 years of the county’s own annual filings to the state — self-reported, desk-reviewed but not audited by OSC. The county does not publish an itemised claims register on its own site — Legislature agendas and minutes carry resolutions only; one county sewer district’s board does list vendor vouchers, in its own minutes (checked 10/05/2026, source). This edition is the filings story: complete, and drillable to the account line. The city edition has a register because North Tonawanda posts its warrants.

On the current reporting basis (2013–2025), revenue exceeded expenditure in 9 of 13 filings. A single-year filing gap is not a deficit claim — fund balance, transfers and capital timing all argue. The county runs roughly 9× North Tonawanda’s budget.

Nine counties, per resident 2025

Each county’s own 2025 filing, divided by its 2020 Census population. Counties differ in what they run — context, not a scorecard.

The property-tax figure is the county levy only — cities, towns, villages and school districts are separate governments on the same parcel.

The county’s sales tax, shared 2024

The county hands a share of its sales tax to every city, town and village inside it, and its filing carries the whole thing as one unlabeled line (A19854 “Distribution of Sales Tax”). It never names the recipients. Their own filings do — the line below is rebuilt from twenty governments’ books.

The county’s distribution line, 1995–2025 — $73,534,274 in 2025

1995200520152025

Filed under account A19854, Distribution of Sales Tax from 2007; not filed under it in the 12 earlier years, which are left blank — a missing filing is shown as missing, never drawn as zero.

The filing also carries funds the adopted budget does not price: CL $1,030,090 · H $26,093,735 · MS $38,161,964 — self-insurance, capital projects and similar are governed outside the budget book, and the H capital fund is one-time by design.

The decisions behind these dollars

The county can’t spend, contract, settle, or move budget money without its Legislature voting on a numbered resolution. This ledger shows where the money went; the register of resolutions is the record of who voted to send it — every one parsed from the county’s own agendas and minutes, votes and all.

Latest meeting with votes read · August 4, 2026 — 61 resolutions, the recorded vote read for 56 of them, and none drew a no.

The method

How it was built

Built exactly like the city edition. Parsed from the Comptroller’s statewide county files — 16,772 account-level rows for Niagara County, 1995–2025 — joined on municipal code (never entity name), flows only, balance-sheet rows excluded. The 2013 schema change is resolved by column name per era and marked on every chart. The build is a gate, not a report: if any year goes missing or a total turns implausible, the generator halts and this page does not update.

✓ BUILD GATES PASS: 31 consecutive years · totals in bounds · schema mapping continuous

Self-reported AFR data: OSC desk-reviews these filings but does not audit them. Peer populations are the 2020 Census (P1). Figures as filed; no inflation adjustment.
